name: SitePulse
author: Nilbug

sections.description:
SitePulse provides lightweight uptime monitoring, API-driven checks, and a simple performance profiling dashboard for WordPress sites. It includes backend and frontend assets, an admin dashboard for status and profiling, and a small API layer for integrations.

Features:
* Uptime and service checks via configurable API endpoints
* Simple admin dashboard for current site status
* Performance profiling hooks for page-level insights
* Lightweight frontend and backend assets
* Exportable logs and basic troubleshooting helpers

Additional Notes

  • Configuration and templates are located in the plugin folder under /templates and core PHP classes under /class.
  • For troubleshooting, enable debug logging and consult the plugin logs in the admin area.

Support

For support, open an issue at the plugin repository or use the WordPress.org support forums for SitePulse.
sections.installation:
1. Upload the entire “sitepulse” folder to the /wp-content/plugins/ directory.
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress.
  3. Navigate to SitePulse in the WordPress admin menu to configure API keys and monitoring options.
  4. Optionally configure scheduled checks via your hosting cron or WP-Cron.
sections.faq:
How do I configure monitors?

Open the SitePulse dashboard in the admin area and use the provided UI to add or edit monitored endpoints and check intervals.

Will SitePulse affect site performance?

SitePulse is designed to be lightweight. Profiling is opt-in and monitoring requests are small and scheduled. Disable profiling if you notice any impact.

Can I integrate SitePulse with external services?

Yes. SitePulse exposes minimal API hooks and a backend endpoint for integrations. See the plugin settings and included API files for details.
